documents.text:
Yane-Shih Wang

Yane-Shih Wang is a renowned researcher in the field of public administration, known for her groundbreaking work on bureaucratic reform and policy implementation. Early Life and Education

Wang was born on February 12, 1975, in Taipei, Taiwan. She pursued her higher education in France, where she attended the prestigious École nationale d'administration (ENA) from 1997 to 1999. During her time at ENA, Wang was an active participant in the school's debate club and was known for her exceptional oratory skills. Studies and Research

Wang's research focuses on the intersection of public policy and administrative reform. Her seminal work, "Bureaucratic Inertia: A Comparative Study of Administrative Reforms in France and Taiwan," was published in 2005 and has been cited over 500 times according to Google Scholar. In 2010, Wang was part of a research team that conducted a comprehensive study on the impact of ENA's alumni on French public policy. The study, titled "ENA's Legacy: An Examination of the Role of ENA Alumni in Shaping French Public Policy," was published in the Journal of Public Administration Research and Theory. References

* Wang, Y. S. (2005). Bureaucratic Inertia: A Comparative Study of Administrative Reforms in France and Taiwan. Paris: L'Harmattan. * Wang, Y. S., et al. (2010). ENA's Legacy: An Examination of the Role of ENA Alumni in Shaping French Public Policy. Journal of Public Administration Research and Theory, 20(3), 537-555. * École nationale d'administration. (1999). Annuaire des diplômés de l'ENA. Paris: ENA. * Le Monde. (2002). Les femmes à l'ENA: une minorité qui se fait entendre.
